fields.summary: Sippy UI fails to render on first load when /sippy-ng URL lacks trailing slash
fields.description:
h2. Summary

When accessing the Sippy UI at a path like `/sippy-ng` (without a trailing slash), the page fails to render on first load. Adding a trailing slash (`/sippy-ng/`) resolves the issue. This is particularly problematic when Sippy is served behind a tunnel or reverse proxy (e.g. cloudflared) where the natural URL does not include the trailing slash.

h2. Details

* The `BrowserRouter` in `index.js` is configured with `basename="/sippy-ng"` (no trailing slash)
* The `package.json` declares `homepage: "/sippy-ng/"` (with trailing slash)
* The Go server-side handler registers on `PathPrefix("/sippy-ng/")` and its SPA fallback rewrites to `/sippy-ng/` (with slash)
* When a user navigates to `/sippy-ng` without the trailing slash, the server's PathPrefix router may not match correctly, or React Router fails to initialize because the request path doesn't match its basename configuration
* The `TestDetailsReport.js` component has an explicit workaround that searches for `/sippy-ng/` in the URL and logs an error if not found: `"No /sippy-ng/ found in URL, this is a bug"`

h2. Expected Behavior

Accessing `/sippy-ng` (without trailing slash) should work identically to `/sippy-ng/` — the server should normalize the path and React Router should render correctly on first load.

h2. Actual Behavior

First page load at `/sippy-ng` (no trailing slash) fails to render the React app. The issue only manifests in certain situations such as first page load, suggesting a race between server-side path rewriting and client-side React Router initialization.



h2. Acceptance Criteria

All routes continue to work, and the non-trailing slash version works to for the FIRST page visit.  Please confirm with playwright.

---
Requested via internal bot
